Load on board: 짐을 자동차에 싣다 (M13's 짐, M50's 자동차). ㄷ-irregular — the family of 듣다 (M2), 걷다 (M6), and 묻다 (M28) gains a fourth member: ㄷ softens to ㄹ before vowels — 실어요, 실었어요. Second job in publishing: 신문에 기사를 싣다 (M8, M48's 기사) — pages carry articles the way trucks carry boxes.

en: to pile up, stack; to build up
notes: Stack it with intent — walls, boxes, snow forts — but Korea keeps its real ledger in the abstract column: 경험을 쌓다 (M33) = build up experience, 실력을 쌓다 — M44 glossed M26's 실력 as 'built skill', and this is the verb that does the building. Careers, trust, and mileage points are all 쌓다-ed one layer at a time. Says 싸타.

쌓다 through M36's passive 이: it piles up on its own, nobody stacking. 눈이 쌓이다 (M11's snow) is the pretty version; 스트레스가 쌓이다 (M14) is the one Korea actually says daily. M53 filed the relief half of the cycle — 피로가 풀리다, M36's 풀리다 untying fatigue; here is the debit side that fills the account first. The badge form 쌓인 (M24) fronts every tired sentence.

en: to yell, let out (a scream); to splurge
notes: 소리를 지르다 (M19) = let out a yell — where M51's 소리치다 launches words at someone, 지르다 launches pure volume: roller coasters, goals, cockroaches. 르-family (M7): 질러요, 질렀어요. Modern wallet slang runs on it too: 질렀다 = I splurged — the shopping cart, screamed at.

Contact, barely made: 손이 닿다 (M8) = within reach — 손이 안 닿는 곳 is where every itch lives, and where stores shelve the expensive things. Hearts make the same contact: 마음이 닿다 (M19) = the feeling got through. Radar: one stroke from M13's 닫다 (close) — 닿다 touches, 닫다 shuts.

en: to reach, extend to; to go crazy
notes: Two dictionary entries, one spelling, both essential. Sense one, reach: 영향을 미치다 (影響 = influence, frozen) is how news-Korean says 'affects', and 생각이 거기까지 미치지 못했어요 = my thinking didn't reach that far. Sense two, mad: 미쳤어? = are you crazy?! — drama-frequent, friends-only; aimed at a stranger it is a genuine insult, so keep it inside 반말 range. Slang has flipped it into praise: 미친 맛 (M18) = insanely good.

A double agent split by hanja. 取 take, in full formal dress: 휴식을 취하다 (休息 = rest, frozen) — the way announcements and doctors say 'get some rest.' 醉 drunk: 술에 취하다 (M9) — 취했어요? = are you drunk? The drunk sense wanders licenseless: 분위기에 취하다 (M26) = drunk on the atmosphere, no bottle required.

en: to exhaust, give one's all; to fulfill
notes: M39's 최선 note already did the arithmetic — '최선을 다하다 = give it everything (다 + 하다: to do-it-all, M9's 다 finally verbing)' — and today the verb stands on its own card: use up completely, carry out fully. 힘을 다해서 (M14) = with everything one has; 책임을 다하다 (M39's 책임) = discharge a duty to the last item. Effort, patience, and phone batteries all eventually 다했다.

屬 belong-속: ~에 속하다 files a thing into its drawer — the taxonomy verb of textbooks and quiz shows. 한국은 아시아에 속해요 (M31's 아시아); 수박은 과일에 속할까요? (M30, M3) — the eternal picnic debate, officially yes. Radar, third 속: M28's 속 is the native deep-inside, 약속's (M5) 속 is bind-束, and this one is membership-屬.

提供 hold-forth-supply: provide, in the register of hotels and terms-of-service. 호텔이 아침 식사를 제공해요 (M23, M3's 식사); 정보를 제공하다 (M33) is the phrasing of every app permission screen you've ever skimmed. M9's 주다 gives person-to-person; 제공하다 supplies — officially, with a logo on it.

考慮 examine-ponder: consider, weigh — the boardroom's thinking verb. 고려해 보겠습니다 (M16's try-machine wearing M49's -겠-) = we will take it into consideration — Korea's politest no; do not hold your breath. Radar: a perfect homophone of 高麗 Goryeo, the dynasty that gave 'Korea' its name — context keeps the kingdom and the committee apart.

M32's 느끼다 through M35's -아/어지다: the feeling arrives on its own, no feeler required. 가을이 느껴져요 (M11) = you can feel autumn in the air; 진심이 느껴졌어요 (M24's 진심) = the sincerity came through. M34's 느낌 is the noun this verb delivers to your door.

M1's 없다 through M35's become-machine: come to not-be-there. 지갑이 없어졌어요 (M21) = my wallet's gone — said at the worst possible moment. Pain, stains, and snack supplies all 없어지다. M35's 사라지다 vanishes with some mystery to it; 없어지다 just stops being where you left it.

M3's 만들다, done unto by M35's machine: be made. 치즈는 우유로 만들어져요 (M40's 치즈, M2's 우유) — (으)로 marks the raw material. Laws, friendships, and new words are all 만들어지다-ed too: the passive voice of the national verb for making.

M1's 크다 + M35's -아/어지다: get bigger — the become-machine's textbook example, finally enrolled. 소리가 점점 커져요 (M19); problems escalate the same way: 문제가 커졌어요 (M7) = this got big. Radar: one vowel from M36's 켜지다 (turn on by itself) — 커지다 grows, 켜지다 lights up.

en: to break out, unfold (events); to widen
notes: The happen-verb of headlines: events break out and unfold on their own — 큰 사건이 벌어졌어요 (M36's 사건). Radar for M56's 벌이다 file (which already tracks 벌다 and 버리다): you 벌이다 the affair; left alone, it 벌어지다-s — launcher and launched. Second sense, gaps: 사이가 벌어지다 (M6's 사이) = a relationship drifts apart — seams, teeth, and friendships all widen with it.

M40's 담다 through M36's passive 기: be held inside. M40 reported that letters, gifts, and songs all claim to be 마음을 담아서 made — 담기다 is how the claim gets inspected: 마음이 담긴 선물 (M19, M9) = a gift with heart actually in it. Bowls do the literal version: 그릇에 담긴 반찬 (M18, M3).

M19's 부르다 through M36's passive 리: be called. The naming frame runs on M32's quote-라고: X라고 불려요 = is called X — how nicknames, titles, and legends get pinned on. Radar: an unrelated 불리다 soaks things — 콩을 불리다 (M40's 콩) = soak the beans overnight; the particle tells you which one showed up.

M56's 발견하다 note promised 'the passive rides free on the 되다-machine (M36): 발견되다' — receipt, paid. Swap the 하다 and the discovery happens TO the thing: 새로운 사실이 발견됐어요 (M35's 새롭다, M24's 사실). The register of museums, headlines, and detective-show epilogues.

進行 advance-go (the parent 진행하다 = to conduct, frozen here): be under way. 회의가 진행되고 있어요 (M10) — meetings, ceremonies, and roadworks are all 진행 중, the sign-language the 사용 중 S2 taught you to read. the swap-the-하다 machine (M36) in its natural habitat: the official announcement.

M10's 사용하다, flipped by the 되다-swap (M36): be used. 이 단어는 요즘 잘 사용되지 않아요 (M10's 단어, M26's 요즘) — the dictionary's polite way of saying 'dated.' You've read 사용 중 on doors since M10; now you can conjugate the other side of the sign.

en: to be thought, be considered (to be)
notes: M10's 생각하다 gone formal-passive: be thought, seem — written Korean holding an opinion at arm's length. ~(으)로 생각됩니다 = it is thought that — the news anchor's shrug, the report's hedge. In speech you'd reach for the 것 같다 hedge (M34); on paper, 생각되다 wears the tie.

M56's 관련 (gate-link) verbed by the 되다-machine: be related to. The working form wears M24's badge: ~와 관련된 = related to ~ — 시험과 관련된 정보 (M10, M33) fronts half the internet's search results. M56 handed you 관련 기사 ready-stacked; now the badge builds itself from any noun you like.
